_source: 59 neuron reconstructions exported from the Little Neural Guide (atlas data: ModelDB packages, NeuroMorpho.Org, Janelia MouseLight / FlyEM / FANC / MANC). Coordinates µm, soma-centred; section = [type 2 axon | 3 dendrite or basal | 4 apical, parent (-1 soma), [x,y,z…], [radius…]]. Morphometrics comp

data.name: CA1 pyramidal cell
data.layer: Soma in stratum pyramidale; basal dendrites in oriens, apical dendrite through radiatum to lacunosum-moleculare
data.how: Filled during whole-cell recording in hippocampal slices, imaged and traced in Neurolucida, with the layer boundaries traced too.
data.role: Main output of the hippocampus. Integrates CA3 input (Schaffer collaterals, middle dendrites) with entorhinal input (distal tuft) and projects to subiculum and entorhinal cortex.
data.cite: Migliore et al. (2018) PLoS Comput Biol 14:e1006423 · ModelDB 244688
data.note: Data-driven multicompartment models; ion-channel densities optimised to each cell’s recordings

data.name: CA1 pyramidal cell
data.how: As above: slice recording, fill and Neurolucida tracing with traced layer boundaries.
data.role: A second CA1 pyramidal cell: real neurons of one type vary a lot in shape, which is why models are fitted per cell.
data.cite: Migliore et al. (2018) PLoS Comput Biol 14:e1006423 · ModelDB 244688
data.note: Same workflow; compare how two cells of one type differ in branching

data.name: CA3b pyramidal cell
data.layer: Soma in stratum pyramidale of CA3b; thorny excrescences on proximal apical dendrites receive mossy-fibre boutons in stratum lucidum
data.how: Recorded in acute hippocampal slices, filled and reconstructed; used to build a compartmental model of CA3b firing classes.
data.role: Receives mossy fibres from dentate granule cells and dense recurrent collaterals from other CA3 cells (thought to support pattern completion), and sends Schaffer collaterals to CA1.
data.note: Explains regular-spiking vs bursting CA3b cells with K⁺ channel densities

data.name: Dentate granule cell
data.layer: Soma in the granule cell layer; dendrites fan out through the molecular layer toward the hippocampal fissure
data.how: Reconstructed in the Claiborne lab (Claiborne archive on NeuroMorpho.Org). Only the dendrites are traced; the axon in the model package was added by the modellers, so it is hidden here.
data.role: First stage of the trisynaptic loop. Receives perforant-path input from entorhinal layer II, fires very sparsely, and drives CA3 through powerful mossy-fibre synapses.
data.note: Granule-cell model built with the TREES toolbox and T2N, validated against rat and mouse data

data.name: Mature dentate granule cell
data.layer: Granule cell layer and molecular layer
data.how: Labelled with an AAV-GFP vector, imaged and reconstructed in Beining et al. (2017). The model’s axon was added by the modellers and is hidden here.
data.role: A second granule cell, from a different lab and labelling method: compare dendritic length and branching with the Claiborne cell.
data.note: Same granule-cell model applied across reconstructions

data.name: CA1 pyramidal cell
data.layer: Basal dendrites in oriens; apical trunk, obliques and tuft through radiatum into lacunosum-moleculare
data.how: Reconstructed CA1 pyramidal neuron from the Spruston lab used in Jarsky et al. (2005). The package adds a separate model axon (not shown). Dendrites only here: the apical tree is the dendA5 subtree in the model files.
data.role: Classic cell for the gating question: does distal entorhinal input matter on its own, or only when paired with CA3 input?
data.cite: Jarsky, Roxin, Kath & Spruston (2005) Nat Neurosci 8:1667–1676 · ModelDB 116084
data.note: Shows that perforant-path dendritic spikes in the tuft reach the soma only when Schaffer input “gates” them

data.name: CA1 pyramidal cell
data.layer: Oriens, radiatum and lacunosum-moleculare; many oblique branches off the apical trunk
data.how: Reconstruction from the Duke–Southampton archive (Turner lab; distributed via L-Neuron / NeuroMorpho.Org), used by Migliore et al. (2005). In the model file the apical trunk and tuft are named “user5” and the obliques “apical_dendrite”; both are shown as apical here. Only a short axon stub is traced.
data.role: Many obliques: a good cell for seeing how branch points load the trunk and attenuate signals.
data.cite: Migliore, Ferrante & Ascoli (2005) J Neurophysiol 94:4145–4155 · ModelDB 55035
data.note: Back- and forward-propagation of action potentials in oblique dendrites depends on local branch geometry and channels

data.name: Dentate granule cell
data.layer: Granule cell layer; dendrites through the molecular layer
data.how: Filled with biocytin during whole-cell recording in hippocampal slices and reconstructed (Schmidt-Hieber, Jonas & Bischofberger 2007). Dendrites only; section 0 is the soma.
data.role: Fitted cable model: a good check on how much perforant-path EPSPs shrink before reaching a granule-cell soma.
data.cite: Schmidt-Hieber, Jonas & Bischofberger (2007) J Neurosci 27:8430–8441 · ModelDB 95960
data.note: Passive cable models fitted to dual soma–dendrite recordings: strong dendritic attenuation, coincidence detection in the soma

data.name: Dentate granule cell
data.layer: Granule cell layer, molecular layer; proximal mossy-fibre axon
data.how: As cell 1, but here the proximal axon was traced too (15 axon sections, the start of the mossy fibre).
data.role: Shows where the mossy-fibre axon leaves the soma, heading toward the hilus and CA3.
data.cite: Schmidt-Hieber, Jonas & Bischofberger (2007) J Neurosci 27:8430–8441 · ModelDB 95960

data.name: DG fast-spiking basket cell
data.layer: Soma at the granule cell layer / hilus border; “apical” dendrites into the molecular layer, “basal” into the hilus; axon in the granule cell layer
data.how: Recorded and filled in hippocampal slices, traced in Neurolucida, imported with NEURON’s Import3D (Nörenberg et al. 2010). Axon fully traced (1302 sections).
data.role: Perisomatic inhibition of granule cells. Its dense axon in the granule cell layer is the “basket” around granule somata.
data.cite: Nörenberg, Hu, Vida, Bartos & Jonas (2010) PNAS 107:894–899 · ModelDB 140789
data.note: Detailed passive models: thick proximal and thin distal dendrites with non-uniform cable properties speed up activation

data.name: PV fast-spiking basket cell
data.layer: Soma near stratum pyramidale; dendrites radial across layers; axon forms baskets around pyramidal cell somata
data.how: Recorded and labelled in vivo by Tukker et al. (2013), reconstructed, and shared through NeuroMorpho.Org. The model authors used the axon of one reconstruction (B13a) for all five models, so the axons shown are shared.
data.role: Perisomatic inhibition of pyramidal cells; paces gamma oscillations and controls spike timing. Reduced PV-cell function is reported in some AD mouse models (Verret et al., 2012).
data.cite: Tzilivaki, Kastellakis & Poirazi (2019) Nat Commun 10:3664 · ModelDB 237595
data.note: Shows that FS basket-cell dendrites integrate inputs non-linearly (“two-stage integrators”)

data.name: PV fast-spiking basket cell
data.how: As above (Tukker et al., 2013, via NeuroMorpho.Org; shared axon B13a).
data.role: Compare its dendrites with Somogyi_1: same class, different shape.
data.cite: Tzilivaki, Kastellakis & Poirazi (2019) Nat Commun 10:3664 · ModelDB 237595
data.note: Second hippocampal FS basket-cell reconstruction from the same model package

data.name: O-LM interneuron
data.layer: Soma and horizontal dendrites in stratum oriens; axon ascends to stratum lacunosum-moleculare
data.how: Reconstructed O-LM cell from earlier work; electrophysiology from mouse O-LM cells (Lawrence et al., 2006). The reconstructions are not the same cells as the recordings.
data.role: Feedback inhibition onto the distal tuft of pyramidal cells, where entorhinal input arrives: O-LM cells gate cortical input and are linked to theta rhythm.
data.cite: Sekulic et al. (2015) Front Synaptic Neurosci 7:2 · ModelDB 182797
data.note: Tests where h-channels sit in O-LM dendrites using multicompartment models

data.name: O-LM interneuron
data.how: As above. The axon of this reconstruction is truncated.
data.role: Dendrites only: compare the horizontal oriens dendrites with the full Starfish reconstruction.
data.cite: Sekulic et al. (2015) Front Synaptic Neurosci 7:2 · ModelDB 182797

data.name: CA1 interneuron
data.how: Slice recording, fill and Neurolucida tracing.
data.role: Classified by firing pattern (e-type) rather than morphological type in the model paper. Most of its tracing is axon, typical of local interneurons.
data.cite: Migliore et al. (2018) PLoS Comput Biol 14:e1006423 · ModelDB 244688
data.note: Modelled as a continuous non-accommodating (cNAC) firing type

data.name: CA1 interneuron
data.how: Slice recording, fill and Neurolucida tracing.
data.role: E-type classification: bursting accommodating.
data.cite: Migliore et al. (2018) PLoS Comput Biol 14:e1006423 · ModelDB 244688

data.name: CA1 interneuron
data.how: Slice recording, fill and Neurolucida tracing.
data.role: Another bAC interneuron: compare axon extent with 011023HP2.
data.cite: Migliore et al. (2018) PLoS Comput Biol 14:e1006423 · ModelDB 244688

data.name: CA1 interneuron
data.how: Slice recording, fill and Neurolucida tracing.
data.role: E-type: continuous accommodating.
data.cite: Migliore et al. (2018) PLoS Comput Biol 14:e1006423 · ModelDB 244688

data.name: CA1 interneuron
data.how: Slice recording, fill and Neurolucida tracing.
data.role: One morphology, two firing-type models: morphology alone does not decide firing pattern.
data.cite: Migliore et al. (2018) PLoS Comput Biol 14:e1006423 · ModelDB 244688
data.note: Used for both a cNAC and a cAC model

data.name: Axo-axonic (chandelier) cell
data.layer: Soma in stratum oriens; axon cartridges along the pyramidal layer
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: Neurobiotin; adult rat (Sprague-Dawley, Male). Reconstructed in Neurolucida; section thickness 70 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Complete, Axon Moderate. Archive: Klausberger (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_35831, TF35-Axo-axonic-cell).
data.role: A real chandelier cell, labelled in vivo in an adult rat (ErbB4+, PV+). Its boutons line up on pyramidal-cell axon initial segments, which is the hippocampal counterpart of the fly GF axo-axonic inputs.

data.name: Axo-axonic (chandelier) cell
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: Biocytin, Alexa 555; young mouse (Nkx2.1Cre-RCE, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Neurolucida; section thickness 400 µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Moderate. Archive: McBain (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_49373, Axoaxonic_cell).
data.role: Mouse chandelier cell from the MGE lineage. Compare the dense cartridge axon with the rat in-vivo cell.

data.name: Axo-axonic (chandelier) cell
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: Neurobiotin; adult rat (Sprague-Dawley, Male). Reconstructed in Neurolucida; section thickness 70 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Complete, Axon Moderate. Archive: Somogyi (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_49814, B10a-1).
data.role: Recorded and labelled in vivo in CA3 (Viney et al. 2013). Axo-axonic cells there fire around theta but are silenced during sharp-wave ripples.

data.name: Axo-axonic (chandelier) cell
data.layer: Inner molecular layer; axon in the granule cell layer
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; young adult rat (VGAT-Venus, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Simple Neurite Tracer; section thickness 300 µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Complete. Archive: Vida (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_252206, Degro_Vidal-cell-38).
data.role: Dentate chandelier cell with a complete axon (Degro et al. 2022). It targets granule-cell axon initial segments.

data.name: Bistratified interneuron
data.layer: Stratum oriens; axon in oriens and radiatum (both sides of the pyramidal layer)
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; adult rat (Wistar, Male). Reconstructed in Simple Neurite Tracer; section thickness 300 µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Moderate. Archive: Beck (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_125756, PD-S-15-02-2011_Z04).
data.role: Bistratified cells inhibit the dendrites that receive CA3 input (oriens and radiatum), in step with the Schaffer collaterals.

data.name: Ivy / neurogliaform cell
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; young mouse (C57BL/6, Not reported). Reconstructed in Neurolucida; section thickness 350 µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Moderate. Archive: Wadiche (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_10845, Fig1E).
data.role: Neurogliaform-family cell with a very dense local axon. These cells release GABA by volume transmission and drive slow GABA-A and GABA-B inhibition.

data.name: CA2 pyramidal cell
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; young mouse (C57BL/6J, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Imaris; section thickness 300 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate. Archive: Dudek (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_112004, Mouse_CA2_Mc_Cell_1).
data.role: CA2 is the small region between CA3 and CA1, important for social memory. Its pyramidal cells resist the plasticity seen in CA1.

data.name: CA1 projection neuron (whole-brain axon)
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: enhanced green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (C57BL/6, Female). Reconstructed in Janelia Workstation-Large Volume Viewer; section thickness 25 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate, Axon Complete. Archive: MouseLight (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_121507, AA0702).
data.role: A Janelia MouseLight reconstruction with the complete axon traced across the whole brain. The local view trims the axon to 800 µm; open the whole-brain page to see all of it.

data.name: CA1 pyramidal cell (complete axon)
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (Pvalb-T2A-CreERT2;Ai166, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Vaa3D; section thickness Not applicable µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Complete. Archive: Peng (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_163712, 18869_5802_x13547_y4406-semi_r).
data.role: SEU–Allen full-morphology reconstruction (Peng et al. 2021): about 100 mm of axon from one cell. Trimmed here to 800 µm.

data.name: CA3 pyramidal cell (complete axon)
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (Pvalb-T2A-CreERT2;Ai166, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Vaa3D; section thickness Not applicable µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Complete. Archive: Peng (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_164632, 18869_4997_x13063_y4444-semi_r).
data.role: About 130 mm of axon from one CA3 cell: recurrent collaterals plus Schaffer collaterals. Trimmed here to 800 µm.

data.name: CA1 VIP-lineage interneuron (complete)
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (Vipr2-IRES2-Cre-neo;Ai166, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Vaa3D; section thickness Not applicable µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Complete. Archive: Peng (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_164347, 18465_00054-semi_r).
data.role: Complete interneuron from the SEU–Allen whole-brain dataset.

data.name: Dentate granule cell (complete mossy fibre)
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: enhanced green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (C57BL/6, Female). Reconstructed in Janelia Workstation-Large Volume Viewer; section thickness 25 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate, Axon Complete. Archive: MouseLight (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_121654, AA0361).
data.role: MouseLight cell with the full mossy-fibre axon traced into CA3. Place it in the brain on the whole-brain page.

data.name: Subicular pyramidal cell (whole-brain axon)
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: enhanced green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (C57BL/6, Female). Reconstructed in Janelia Workstation-Large Volume Viewer; section thickness 25 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate, Axon Complete. Archive: MouseLight (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_121817, AA0560).
data.role: The subiculum is the main output of the hippocampus. This axon (about 60 mm) leaves the hippocampal formation.

data.name: Lateral entorhinal projection neuron
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: enhanced green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (C57BL/6, Female). Reconstructed in Janelia Workstation-Large Volume Viewer; section thickness 25 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate, Axon Complete. Archive: MouseLight (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_121938, AA1002).
data.role: About 290 mm of axon. In the CCF check, 60% of its sampled axon lies in the dentate gyrus and 15% in CA3: this is the perforant path, in a single real cell.

data.name: Entorhinal pyramidal cell · wild type
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: Golgi-Cox; adult mouse (C57BL/6, Male). Reconstructed in Amira; section thickness 50 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Complete. Archive: Zhang_Jiang (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_158995, WT0601-Ect-R-8451-fiber03).
data.role: Control cell for the 3xTg-AD comparison (Zhang/Jiang lab). Compare dendritic length and branching with the AD-model cell next to it.

data.name: Entorhinal pyramidal cell · 3xTg-AD
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: Golgi-Cox; adult mouse (3 x Tg-AD, Male). Reconstructed in Amira; section thickness 50 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Complete. Archive: Zhang_Jiang (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_158996, AD0602-Ect-L-8511-fiber02).
data.role: From the 3xTg-AD Alzheimer’s mouse model. One pair cannot show a group effect, but it shows the kind of measurement (dendritic length, branch number) used in AD morphology studies.

data.name: MEC fast-spiking PV basket cell
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; young adult rat (VGAT-Venus, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Simple Neurite Tracer; section thickness 300 µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Moderate. Archive: Barreda (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_176949, M_F_5).
data.role: Fast-spiking PV interneuron from MEC layer 2/3, the circuit that holds grid cells. Cells like this provide fast perisomatic inhibition and support gamma rhythms.

data.name: Medial septum PV / HCN4 neuron
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: horseradish peroxidase + diaminobenzidine; adult rat (Sprague-Dawley, Male). Reconstructed in Neurolucida; section thickness 70 µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Moderate. Archive: Somogyi (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_104696, Unal-Somogyi-2018-D55c).
data.role: A GABAergic “theta pacemaker” projection neuron, labelled in vivo. Its axon targets hippocampal interneurons, and HCN4 is the h-channel isoform. This links directly to the resonance lessons.

data.name: Thalamocortical neuron (VPM, complete axon)
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (Tnnt1-IRES2-CreERT2;Ai82;Ai140, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Vaa3D; section thickness Not applicable µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Complete. Archive: Peng (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_163604, 18454_01106-semi_f).
data.role: Whisker-relay thalamic neuron from the SEU–Allen full-morphology dataset. Its axon targets barrel cortex.

data.name: Thalamocortical neuron (VPL, whole-brain axon)
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: enhanced green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (C57BL/6, Female). Reconstructed in Janelia Workstation-Large Volume Viewer; section thickness 25 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate, Axon Complete. Archive: MouseLight (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_121515, AA0322).
data.role: MouseLight reconstruction. In the CCF check, 93% of its sampled axon is in isocortex.

data.name: M1 layer 2/3 pyramidal cell (whole-brain axon)
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: enhanced green fluorescent protein; adult mouse (C57BL/6, Female). Reconstructed in Janelia Workstation-Large Volume Viewer; section thickness 25 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate, Axon Complete. Archive: MouseLight (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_121510, AA0884).
data.role: MouseLight cell projecting across cortex (81%) and into striatum (14%).

data.name: Human cortical pyramidal cell (Allen)
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; adult human (Not applicable, Male). Reconstructed in Vaa3D; section thickness 350 µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Moderate. Archive: Allen Cell Types (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_102401, H17-03-011-11-04-05_650978964_m).
data.role: From the Allen Cell Types Database: a living human neuron recorded in slices from resected tissue, then reconstructed.
data.cite: Allen Cell Types · NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_102401 · doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2016.10.019

data.name: Human cortical interneuron (Allen)
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; adult human (Not applicable, Female). Reconstructed in Vaa3D; section thickness 350 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Complete, Axon Incomplete. Archive: Allen Cell Types (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_102399, H17-03-010-11-13-01_656411100_m).
data.role: Allen Cell Types aspiny (inhibitory) human neuron. The axon is incomplete.
data.cite: Allen Cell Types · NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_102399 · doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2016.10.019

data.name: Mouse V1 layer 4 interneuron (Allen)
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; adult mouse (Chat-IRES-Cre-neo, Female). Reconstructed in Vaa3D; section thickness 350 µm. Completeness: Dendrites & Axon Moderate. Archive: Allen Cell Types (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_102367, Chat-IRES-Cre-neo_Ai14-287662-04-02-01_614444566_m).
data.role: From the Allen Cell Types mouse dataset (Chat-Cre line): patch-clamp recording plus reconstruction, part of a standardised pipeline.
data.cite: Allen Cell Types · NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_102367 · doi:10.1016/j.neuron.2015.02.022

data.name: Cerebellar Purkinje cell
data.layer: Purkinje layer; flat fan-shaped dendrite in the molecular layer
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biocytin; young adult mouse (C56BL/6, Not reported). Reconstructed in NeuronStudio; section thickness 250 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Complete. Archive: Dusart (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_10069, Purkinje-slice-ageP43-6).
data.role: The most elaborate dendrite in the brain, receiving well over 100,000 parallel-fibre synapses (rat estimates are about 150,000–175,000) and input from a single climbing fibre.

data.name: Medium spiny neuron
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: Golgi-Cox; not reported rat (Sprague-Dawley, Male). Reconstructed in Custom; section thickness 90 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Complete, Axon Incomplete. Archive: Spiga (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_10032, MSN-shell).
data.role: MSNs are GABAergic projection neurons and make up about 95% of striatal neurons. Dendrites only.

data.name: Olfactory bulb mitral cell
data.layer: Main olfactory bulb; apical tuft in one glomerulus
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: biotinylated dextran amine; adult mouse (C57BL/6, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Neurolucida; section thickness 310 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate, Axon Incomplete. Archive: Igarashi (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_111356, TM6).
data.role: Its single apical dendrite ends in one glomerulus and its long lateral dendrites run through the external plexiform layer.

data.name: Spinal motoneuron (cat)
data.layer: Cervical spinal cord C3, ventral horn
data.how: In vivo labelling; stain: Neurobiotin; adult cat (Not reported, Female). Reconstructed in Neurolucida; section thickness 50 µm. Completeness: Dendrites Complete. Archive: Rose (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_34000, SPLENIUS-SENA331).
data.role: A very large dendritic tree (about 100 mm) from an in-vivo fill. The classic Rall cable-theory cell type.

data.name: Direction-selective retinal ganglion cell
data.how: In vitro slice preparation; stain: Alexa Fluor 488; adult mouse (Sema6-/-, Male/Female). Reconstructed in Neurolucida; section thickness Not applicable µm. Completeness: Dendrites Moderate. Archive: Feller (NeuroMorpho.Org NMO_102966, 160427_pair1dsgc).
data.role: Flagged: this cell comes from a Sema6 knockout (a developmental-wiring study), so it is not wild type.

data.name: Olfactory projection neuron (DA1, fly)
data.layer: Antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 → mushroom-body calyx → lateral horn
data.how: Electron-microscopy connectome (Janelia FlyEM hemibrain v1.x; Scheffer et al. 2020), body 754534424, DA1_lPN_R, cell-body fiber AVM02. Skeleton from the navis example data (8 nm voxels → µm). 646 presynaptic and 2364 postsynaptic sites in the skeleton’s synapse table.
data.role: Carries the pheromone (cVA) channel from antennal-lobe glomerulus DA1 to the mushroom body and lateral horn. In EM there is no soma–dendrite–axon staining, so every branch here is shown as neurite.

data.name: Olfactory projection neuron (DA1, fly)
data.layer: Antennal lobe glomerulus DA1 → mushroom-body calyx → lateral horn
data.how: Electron-microscopy connectome (Janelia FlyEM hemibrain v1.x; Scheffer et al. 2020), body 722817260, DA1_lPN_R, cell-body fiber AVM02. Skeleton from the navis example data (8 nm voxels → µm). 701 presynaptic and 2435 postsynaptic sites in the skeleton’s synapse table.
data.role: Carries the pheromone (cVA) channel from antennal-lobe glomerulus DA1 to the mushroom body and lateral horn. In EM there is no soma–dendrite–axon staining, so every branch here is shown as neurite.

data.name: Spinal α-motoneuron (lumbar, cat)
data.layer: Lumbar ventral horn (lamina IX) · triceps surae (calf) motor pool
data.how: Intracellular HRP fill in vivo, reconstructed in 3D (NeuroMorpho.Org, Burke archive; Cullheim, Fleshman, Glenn & Burke 1987). Imported from the NEURON files of Balbi et al. 2015 (ModelDB 180370). Axon hillock and initial segment use the package dimensions; the myelinated motor axon is left out. The package gives the soma as a 120 µm placeholder cylinder; it is drawn and modelled here as a 55 µm sphere-equivalent disc, typical for cat α-motoneurons.
data.role: A lower motor neuron: its axon leaves the cord in the ventral root and makes one motor unit in a leg muscle. The same cell type drives the quadriceps in the knee jerk and the calf in the ankle jerk, recruits by size (Henneman) as you push harder, and is the cell lost in ALS. Its dendrites (about 80–110 mm in total) take in thousands of synapses, including the Ia afferents of the stretch reflex.

data.name: Spinal α-motoneuron (lumbar, cat)
data.layer: Lumbar ventral horn (lamina IX) · triceps surae (calf) motor pool
data.how: Intracellular HRP fill in vivo, reconstructed in 3D (NeuroMorpho.Org, Burke archive; Cullheim, Fleshman, Glenn & Burke 1987). Imported from the NEURON files of Balbi et al. 2015 (ModelDB 180370). Axon hillock and initial segment use the package dimensions; the myelinated motor axon is left out. The package gives the soma as a 98 µm placeholder cylinder; it is drawn and modelled here as a 55 µm sphere-equivalent disc, typical for cat α-motoneurons.
data.role: A lower motor neuron: its axon leaves the cord in the ventral root and makes one motor unit in a leg muscle. The same cell type drives the quadriceps in the knee jerk and the calf in the ankle jerk, recruits by size (Henneman) as you push harder, and is the cell lost in ALS. Its dendrites (about 80–110 mm in total) take in thousands of synapses, including the Ia afferents of the stretch reflex.

data.name: Spinal α-motoneuron (lumbar, cat)
data.how: Intracellular fill in vivo, 3D reconstruction from NeuroMorpho.Org. Imported from the NEURON files of Balbi et al. 2015 (ModelDB 180370). Axon hillock and initial segment use the package dimensions; the myelinated motor axon is left out.
data.role: A lower motor neuron: its axon leaves the cord in the ventral root and makes one motor unit in a leg muscle. The same cell type drives the quadriceps in the knee jerk and the calf in the ankle jerk, recruits by size (Henneman) as you push harder, and is the cell lost in ALS. Its dendrites (about 80–110 mm in total) take in thousands of synapses, including the Ia afferents of the stretch reflex.

data.name: Layer 5 thick-tufted pyramidal cell (pyramidal-tract type)
data.how: Biocytin fill in an acute slice, 3D reconstruction used by Hay, Hill, Schürmann, Markram & Segev 2011 (ModelDB 139653, cell1).
data.role: The class of cortical neuron whose axon leaves the cortex for the brainstem and spinal cord. In motor cortex these are the corticospinal “upper motor neurons” (the giant human versions are Betz cells); in primates, including humans, some synapse directly on spinal α-motoneurons, which is what makes skilled finger movements possible. This one is from rat sensory cortex, so treat it as a stand-in for the cell type.

data.name: Human layer 2/3 pyramidal cell
data.layer: Human temporal cortex, layers 2/3 (tissue from epilepsy surgery)
data.how: Recorded and biocytin-filled in slices of living human cortex removed during neurosurgery, then reconstructed (Eyal et al. 2016, ModelDB 195667).
data.role: Human L2/3 pyramidal cells are larger and have longer, more branched dendrites than rodent ones, and Eyal et al. showed they couple synaptic input to the soma more effectively. Compare it with the rat L5 cell and the CA1 cells.

data.name: Tergotrochanteral motor neuron (TTMn, fly)
data.how: Electron-microscopy reconstruction in the Female Adult Nerve Cord (FANC; Phelps, Hildebrand, Graham et al. 2021), from the public data release (github.com/htem/GridTape_VNC_paper), nm → µm. The release traces the soma, primary neurite, main branches and the axon to the nerve, not every fine twig; diameters are not in the release, so the main neurite and axon are set to 4 µm and side branches to 1.6 µm (assigned, not measured). The soma size is from the tracing.
data.role: Drives the jump muscle (TTM) in the escape take-off. The giant fiber makes a mixed electrical (ShakB gap junction) and cholinergic synapse onto its dendrite in the mesothoracic neuromere, which is why the jump follows a GF spike within about 0.8 ms.

data.name: Peripherally synapsing interneuron (PSI, fly)
data.how: Electron-microscopy reconstruction in the Female Adult Nerve Cord (FANC; Phelps, Hildebrand, Graham et al. 2021), from the public data release (github.com/htem/GridTape_VNC_paper), nm → µm. The release traces the soma, primary neurite, main branches and the axon to the nerve, not every fine twig; diameters are not in the release, so the main neurite and axon are set to 3 µm and side branches to 1.2 µm (assigned, not measured). The soma size is from the tracing.
data.role: Relays the giant fiber to the flight-muscle motor neurons: GF → PSI (electrical) → DLM motor neurons (cholinergic). Its name comes from synapsing on motor-neuron axons outside the neuropil, in the nerve.

data.name: Wing motor neuron, PDMN nerve (fly)
data.how: Electron-microscopy reconstruction in the Female Adult Nerve Cord (FANC; Phelps, Hildebrand, Graham et al. 2021), from the public data release (github.com/htem/GridTape_VNC_paper), nm → µm. The release traces the soma, primary neurite, main branches and the axon to the nerve, not every fine twig; diameters are not in the release, so the main neurite and axon are set to 3 µm and side branches to 1.2 µm (assigned, not measured). The soma size is from the tracing.
data.role: One of the seven motor neurons in the posterior dorsal mesothoracic nerve, the nerve that carries the DLM (indirect flight muscle) motor neurons that PSI drives. FANC does not say which of the seven this one is, so use it as a DLM-type motor neuron stand-in.

data.name: Giant fiber (DNp01) axon, fly
data.layer: Neck connective → mesothoracic neuromere (ventral nerve cord)
data.how: Not a tracing. The thoracic part follows the real MANC v1.2.1 synapse positions on GF body 10000 (1,549 synapses from your gf_axo-axonic export): the centreline is the median synapse position in 10 µm steps along their long axis (359 µm). Above it, 300 µm of straight neck connective; the brain (soma and dendrites) is replaced by a small node at the top so the cell can be driven. Axon diameter 10 µm, as in the guide's calibrated giant fiber model.
data.role: The largest axon in the fly. A looming stimulus fires it, and one spike travels down the neck connective to the thoracic ganglion, where it drives the TTMn (jump) and, through PSI, the DLM flight-muscle motor neurons: the escape take-off. Wire it to the TTMn and PSI in the circuit builder.
